From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 15 Nov 2025 13:12:00 -0500
Subject: MAP: Glider AI evaluation — kickoff & technical leads

Ethan —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As discussed, attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (Glider_MAP_v1.xlsx) to frame the evaluation and proposed close timeline. I wanted to loop in our SE and AM so we can align on technical owners and success criteria before we lock the schedule.

Quick summary / asks: 
- Goal: 2-week evaluation of Redwood inference for throughput/latency and integration compatibility, leading to PO by end of December.
- Technical lead (Redwood SE): Dev Patel (cc'd).
- Customer engineering lead: can you confirm who on your side will own test harness, infra, and security reviews?
- Success criteria we propose: throughput >= 250 qps for 128-token median, 95th percentile latency < 120ms, compatibility with your prefix-caching approach.

Proposed immediate next steps (week 1):
1) Kickoff call with SE + your eng lead (30-45m) — propose Tue 18 Nov, 10:00–10:45 ET.
2) Access & test data: your test endpoints + sample prompts by EOD Wed.
3) Security questionnaire (attached) — aim to complete by Fri.

Dev — high level on the MAP and the proposed criteria; feel free to add technical asks in the thread.

Ethan/Dana — if different folks should be on the kickoff, please let us know and we’ll update the invite.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Exec | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Glider_MAP_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), glider-security-ask.pdf (PDF)

Thanks Karthik — appreciate the clear plan.

On our side: I will own the evaluation as engineering lead. Dana (cc'd) will drive security/compliance follow-ups. Additional internal stakeholders to loop in for the kickoff: 
- Priya Kothari (Platform) — will validate infra constraints / VPC routing
- Miguel Santos (SRE) — will help run load tests

Tue 18 Nov at 10:00 ET works for us. Two small asks before the call: 
- Can Dev share a short checklist of environment variables/ports we need to open?
- Any model variants we should expect to test (FP16, Q4_0)?

I reviewed the MAP briefly — looks good. We will push a calendar invite for Tue and share a link to our test harness.

Best,

Ethan — thanks, looking forward to the call. Quick technical notes to help your team prep: 

1) Network & access checklist (short):
- Allow outbound TLS on ports 443 and 8443 from your test hosts to our inference endpoints.
- If you plan on running private deployment, we will need an ingress rule to our test VPC peering (details on call).

2) Model variants we recommend testing (order of priority):
- redwood-tiny-q4_0 (fastest / baseline)
- redwood-base-fp16 (quality baseline)
- redwood-safety-optimized (for PII-sensitive prompts)

3) Data & harness: please provide a set of 500 representative prompts and 20 high-concurrency test scenarios. We can run an initial synthetic sweep to establish baseline throughput and then run your harness for validation.

4) Dev environment creds: we prefer temporary API key + IP allowlist. If you need a long-lived service account for CI, flag that and we’ll escalate.

I’ll prepare a 10-minute demo of the test harness and where to find kernel/runtime logs that matter for tail latency analysis.

—Dev
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
